First, I should consider why she gets sleepy. Is it because of her age, or maybe she has some health issues that make her tired more easily? If she's getting sleepy, maybe she needs rest, and spending too much time with her could be exhausting for her. On the other hand, I want to make sure she feels loved and cared for, so visiting her is important. But then, if I only visit for an hour, is that enough? Maybe she would appreciate longer visits, but if she's getting sleepy, maybe she doesn't want to be awake for too long. I'm a bit confused here. How do I balance her need for rest with my desire to spend time with her? I also wonder if there are other ways to show her I care besides just visiting. Maybe sending her letters or calling her on the phone could help. But I think visiting in person is special because she can see me and we can interact face-to-face. Another thing to think about is how she feels about the visits. Does she seem happy when I come, or does she seem tired and ready for me to leave? If she's happy, maybe the hour is enough. But if she seems like she wants me to stay longer, maybe I should adjust my schedule to spend more time with her. I also need to consider my own feelings. If I feel like I'm not spending enough time with her, that could make me feel guilty or sad. So, it's important to find a balance that works for both of us. Maybe I can talk to the nursing home staff to get some advice. They might have insights into how much time is appropriate for her given her health condition. They could also suggest other ways to support her that don't involve long visits. I also wonder if there are other family members who can help with visiting her. If I can coordinate with them, maybe we can take turns visiting her so she gets more time with different people, but without exhausting her. In the end, I think the most important thing is to make sure she feels loved and supported. Whether that means short visits or longer ones, as long as she feels cared for, that's what matters. But I also need to respect her need for rest and not push her beyond what she can handle. So, to sum it up, visiting her for an hour because she gets sleepy seems like a reasonable approach. It balances her need for rest with my ability to spend quality time with her. But I should also keep an eye on how she feels and adjust as needed to make sure she's comfortable and happy.
